structured_output.summary:
I changed one file, src/optimizer/deliminator.cpp. Deliminator::Optimize keeps the deepest join with the DelimGet when the left side has a selection. It now skips that when two things are true: the delim join is SEMI or ANTI, and its right subtree has no blocking or deduplicating operator. The operators checked are aggregate/group-by, window, limit, order-by, top-n, distinct, and a nested delim join. A new file-local static recursive helper, HasBlockingOperator, does that check; no header changed. In those cases the plan falls back to the existing removal path, the one already used when the left side has no selection. EXISTS and NOT EXISTS then become a single hash SEMI/ANTI join.

Bench (your build vs current best, two runs):
- q04: 325.9 → 224.1ms (-31.2%), then 292.7 → 203.7ms (-30.4%).
- q22: 172.2 → 141.6ms (-17.8%), then 169.9 → 131.9ms (-22.4%).
- Geomean: -4.6% over all visible templates.
- The first full run showed q16 at +11.6% and q19 at +9.5%. Neither has a correlated subquery, so this change can't touch their plans. On rerun they came in at -1.7% and +3.2%, so it was noise.

The q04 profile now shows a single HASH_JOIN RIGHT_SEMI between the filtered orders scan and lineitem, with no RIGHT_DELIM_JOIN, DELIM_SCAN or dedup HASH_GROUP_BY. I checked small hand-built inputs against hand-worked answers, and all were correct:
- NOT EXISTS with NULL keys on both sides
- EXISTS and NOT EXISTS with an extra correlated inequality
- NOT EXISTS with an IS NOT DISTINCT FROM correlation
structured_output.generality:
This helps correlated EXISTS / NOT EXISTS subqueries when the outer table is filtered and the subquery body is only scans, filters, projections and joins. The outer filter used to make the optimizer keep a delim join plus a duplicate-eliminated scan, which a single semi/anti join does no better. It does not apply to:
- MARK joins (IN / NOT IN with a subquery, ANY/ALL) or SINGLE joins (scalar subqueries)
- subqueries containing an aggregate, window, limit, order-by, top-n, distinct or a nested delim join, which keep the old behaviour
- outer queries with no filter, which were already deliminated before this change

The case that could get slower is a right side made of a long join chain, where the kept inner join with the delim set used to filter early. If that shows up, tighten the check to also forbid joins on the right side.
structured_output.notes: The q04 semi join's condition is still `o_orderkey IS NOT DISTINCT FROM o_orderkey`, inherited from the delim join. The lineitem scan shows no dynamic or bloom filter pushed down from the semi join's build side. A follow-up could turn NOT DISTINCT FROM into plain equality for SEMI joins, which is safe for SEMI because a NULL outer key never matches under EXISTS semantics. It is not safe for ANTI with no IS NOT NULL handling, so be careful there. That could let a join filter or min-max filter prune the large probe-side scan, which still costs about 1.9s of cumulative scan time in q04. I didn't try MARK joins, since the issue scoped them out.
